Elaine: Heads-up — planning a targeted admin entitlement prune for remote-service accounts next Tue (will run as a staged canary across 3 orgs).
Sam: sgtm. what's the scope? specific roles or all admin-capable roles?
Elaine: Start narrow: svc-* principals with iam:Admin-like bindings + any owner-like KMS grants. We'll iterate.
Marta: Can you drop the exact query you'll run for KMS grants? need to verify I can reproduce in staging.
Elaine: Yep. Quick grep of CloudTrail/KMS audit logs then cross-ref with IAM bindings. Example AWS CLI snippet:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue="arn:aws:kms:..." --max-results 50
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --limit 100
```
Elaine: We'll also run a permissions-scan that looks for principals with UpdateKey/GenerateDataKey permissions.
Jay: How do we handle short-lived approvals if someone needs an admin during the prune? JIT?
Priya: Yes — use the JIT grant flow (time-limited role). Add a manual approval step in the runbook and log request ids to the ticket.
Noah: Oncall note: make sure pruning work adds an announcement to #eng-oncall 10m before each canary batch.
Sam: Any vuln or active incident dependency? don't want to drop something that was elevated for triage.
Elaine: Good point. We'll query open incident tags and exclude any principal referenced in a currently open incident or vuln ticket.
Elaine: Plan (high-level):
• Weekday 1: dry-run report (no changes) + owner outreach for top-50 suspects
• Weekday 2: canary prune (5% of matches) with rollback hooks, monitor 1h
• Weekday 3: expand to 25% if no regressions
• Weekday 4+: full sweep with staggered windows
Marta: What's the rollback hook look like? are we automating re-attach or just logging steps?
Elaine: We'll automate temporary rebind via stored terraform state snapshot + a fast reprovision script, but also document manual steps. Rollback tag will be created in the audit log with reason and runbook link.
Sam: Need a safe way to test service accounts that aren't human-owned. Can we run a smoke pipeline that exercises core paths post-prune?
Priya: I can add an automated smoke-check using our integration harness (k8s jobs + healthcheck endpoint). Failures create an auto-rollback ticket.
Jay: Who is owner for the remote-service group? want to ping them early.
Elaine: Owners: @Marta for infra svc, @Sam for platform svc. I'll DM the rest — also pinging @Noah for oncall coverage.
AuditBot: Audit log retention set to 400 days for KMS events. All prune actions will include a unique audit_id.
Noah: schedule wise — can we target 03:00 UTC to minimize traffic? aligns with low usage for EU/US.
Elaine: Yes 03:00 UTC for canary. I'll create a calendar invite and ticket: INFRA-4321.
Sam: Please add a quick repro checklist to the ticket: affected principal list, exact change diff, smoke results, rollback id.
Elaine: Will do. Also adding a watch on throttling/latency metrics for the runtime queues — changes might affect token signing calls.
Priya: Also reminder: KMS key policy changes need customer-facing communication if customer keys are touched. We'll exclude any customer-managed keys unless explicitly approved.
Marta: For the dry-run, can we get a CSV with columns: principal, role, last_activity_ts, owner, suggested_action? that'll help owners triage.
Elaine: Yep — dry-run output will be CSV + human-friendly digest. Last-activity derived from last successful auth via audit logs.
Jay: One more ask: include a flag in the runbook to skip any principal with recent MFA bypass escalations (we had one last month).
Elaine: Added. Also tagging a vuln thread: I found 2 orphaned grants on a deprecated key during preliminary scan — created ticket SEC-2910 and flagged for immediate cleanup after approvals.
Priya: SEC-2910 acked. we'll coordinate with apps team to verify no active use.
Noah: During canary, I'll be watching error budgets and will handle immediate rollbacks if we see >0.5% ERROR spike in auth errors.
Sam: Cool. post-prune, let's run a randomized sampling of 500 endpoints to ensure no silent failures.
Elaine: Final: I'll post the runbook link and attach the dry-run CSV by EOD Fri. ping me if you want early access to the list.
Marta: Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness.
Priya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
